issues.description: The problem statement says pixels are rounded to 32 bits per pixel (lines 17-18) but then states "Die Pixel sind als Array von 64-Bit Werten (Quadwords) organisiert." (lines 21-22). The template and solution both treat pixels as 32-bit (4 bytes) each: display_start is allocated as 8,294,400 bytes (which matches 1920×1080×4) in the template (display_start RESB 8294400), and the solution multiplies coordinates by 4 (mov edx, 4; mul edx / mov edi, 4; mul edi / uses 7680 = 1920*4) and writes a 32-bit value (mov [addr], ecx). This contradiction (problem says 64-bit but code uses 32-bit) will directly confuse students when they compute addresses (using *8 for quadwords vs *4 used in provided code) and can cause incorrect implementations or wrong answers.
issues.suggested_fix: Resolve the mismatch between the text and the code. The least disruptive fix is to correct the problem statement to state that pixels are 32-bit (4 bytes, doublewords) rather than 64-bit quadwords — e.g. change "Die Pixel sind als Array von 64-Bit Werten (Quadwords) organisiert." to "Die Pixel sind als Array von 32-Bit Werten (Doublewords) organisiert." Alternatively, if the intent was truly 64-bit pixels, update the template and solution to allocate display_start for 1920×1080×8 bytes and change address calculations to multiply by 8 (and adjust constants accordingly) and store 64-bit values — but this is a larger change and also requires adjusting how color values (ecx) are handled.
